title: How do five related divisions share one long division?
description: A hundred and twenty six is divided by eight with a long division. The four smaller numbers are each that number divided by ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand, so each answer is divided the same way. Multiplying back checks one answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: do one long division, then slide the decimal point to match how much smaller the number is. Watch for students who slide the point the wrong number of places.

video_script.why: The child can do one long division but redoes the whole division for each smaller number and slips with the decimal point.
video_script.substitution: Each smaller number is a hundred and twenty six divided by ten, a hundred, a thousand or ten thousand, so the answer slides the point the same number of places.
video_script.anchor: A hundred and twenty six, twelve point six, one point two six, zero point one two six and zero point zero one two six, each divided by eight
video_script.payoff_line: The last answer is zero point zero zero one five seven five.

final_answer.spoken: fifteen point seven five, one point five seven five, zero point one five seven five, zero point zero one five seven five and zero point zero zero one five seven five

maths_rules: 126 / 8: 126 Ones / 8 = 15 Ones rem 6; 6 Ones = 60 Tenths; 60 / 8 = 7 Tenths rem 4; 4 Tenths = 40 Hundredths; 40 / 8 = 5 Hundredths, so 15.75
video_script.design: The five divisions stay on the board; one long division is done once and the point slides one, two, three and four places left.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; five divisions in a row: 126 ÷ 8, 12.6 ÷ 8, 1.26 ÷ 8, 0.126 ÷ 8, 0.0126 ÷ 8, each with an empty answer box
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about dividing by eight.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first three numbers are a hundred and twenty six, twelve point six and one point two six.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last two are zero point one two six and zero point zero one two six. Each is divided by eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is each quotient?

beats.on_screen: the five divisions and their empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 126, 12.6, 1.26, 0.126, 0.0126 in a row; the decimal point slides one more place left each time

marks.row: the five numbers are lined up with their decimal points
marks.slide: the point slides one more place left each time, so each number is ten times smaller

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book. Do one long division first.
<bookmark mark='slide'/>Each number after it is ten times smaller than the one before. Each answer is ten times smaller too.

marks.given: the first three divisions are written
marks.given2: the last two divisions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five numbers to be divided by eight. A hundred and twenty six, twelve point six and one point two six. <bookmark mark='given2'/>Then zero point one two six and zero point zero one two six.

marks.find: the five answer boxes are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the quotient of each division.

marks.s1a: 126 ÷ 8 is set in a long division frame
marks.s1b: fifteen Ones go to the answer and six Ones remain

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, a long division of a hundred and twenty six by eight.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>A hundred and twenty six divided by eight gives fifteen Ones, and six Ones remain.

beats.on_screen: decimal point placed; 6 Ones = 60 Tenths; 60 Tenths ÷ 8 = 7 Tenths, 4 Tenths remain; 4 Tenths = 40 Hundredths; 40 Hundredths ÷ 8 = 5 Hundredths; 126 ÷ 8 = 15.75

marks.s2a: the point is placed and the six Ones regroup into sixty Tenths
marks.s2b: seven Tenths go to the answer and four Tenths remain
marks.s2c: the four Tenths regroup into forty Hundredths and five go to the answer

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, place the decimal point. Regroup the six Ones into sixty Tenths.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Sixty Tenths divided by eight gives seven Tenths, and four Tenths remain.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Regroup them into forty Hundredths. Forty Hundredths divided by eight gives five Hundredths. The answer is fifteen point seven five.

marks.s3b: 15.75 ÷ 10 is written and the point slides one place left to give 1.575
marks.s3d: 15.75 ÷ 100 is written and the point slides two places left to give 0.1575

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, twelve point six is a hundred and twenty six divided by ten.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Divide fifteen point seven five by ten, and we get one point five seven five.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>One point two six is a hundred and twenty six divided by a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s3d'/>Divide fifteen point seven five by a hundred, and we get zero point one five seven five.

marks.s4b: 15.75 ÷ 1000 is written and the point slides three places left to give 0.01575

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, zero point one two six is a hundred and twenty six divided by a thousand.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Divide fifteen point seven five by a thousand. We get zero point zero one five seven five.

marks.s5b: 15.75 ÷ 10000 is written with the decimal left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Step five, zero point zero one two six is a hundred and twenty six divided by ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>Divide fifteen point seven five by ten thousand. The point slides four places left.

marks.s6b: the product 12.6 is matched with the number in 12.6 ÷ 8

narration: <bookmark mark='s6a'/>Step six, check by multiplying back. One point five seven five times eight is twelve point six.
<bookmark mark='s6b'/>That matches the number in the second division.

marks.rest: the first two other answers are boxed
marks.rest2: the next two other answers are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The last answer is zero point zero zero one five seven five.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other four are fifteen point seven five and one point five seven five. <bookmark mark='rest2'/>Then zero point one five seven five and zero point zero one five seven five.
